reuse.why: Reuses getApproxNumberThreshold and getRangeAmount and routes server sites through one function, but adds a new getExpectedAmount beside the existing getScheduledAmount (which already covered missing/number/range) instead of extending it, leaving two near-equivalent entry points.

duplication.why: Removes the inline null/number/range ternaries in schedules/app.ts, schedule-template and forecast, but computeSchedulePreviewTransactions keeps its own null/number dispatch around the new helper and getScheduledAmount now just wraps getExpectedAmount.

placement.why: The rule lives in shared/schedules.ts next to getRangeAmount and reuses the tolerance from shared/rules.

scope.why: Edits are confined to the amount-rule sites and a test.

maintainability.why: The operator is an optional trailing parameter, so the rule applies only where a caller remembers to pass it (several getScheduledAmount callers do not, and the preview site's local dispatch skips it for every numeric amount), which makes it easy to drift.

bypasses_abstraction.where: shared/schedules.ts computeSchedulePreviewTransactions keeps `_amount == null ? 0 : typeof number ? _amount : getExpectedAmount(...)`, so numeric approximate amounts never reach the helper.

disguised_duplication.where: getScheduledAmount and the new getExpectedAmount are the same decision split into two exported functions; the preview site's missing/number dispatch duplicates the helper's own branches.

one_place.where: The rule is in getExpectedAmount, but it is opt-in via an optional op argument: computeSchedulePreviewTransactions bypasses it for numbers, getScheduledAmount callers in SchedulesTable/mobile/useScheduleEdit pass no op, and forecast-schedules computes its own op fallback.
